text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Confusion settles over aid mission: Planned relief effort in Zaire may be 'completely reoriented,' Canadian Defense Minister says.
- Canadian forces stalled in Uganda: Rwandan officials denying clearance.
- Tories triumph in Prince Edward Island election: Victory their first in decade.
- Tougher sentences sought for young: Task force urges transfers to adult court.
- No drug testing done at university bowl games: Canadian InterUniversity Athletic Union denies asking doping-control group to stay away.
- Tobacco crackdown looms: Big fight seen over law coming Thursday that would ban ads, curtail sponsorships.
- Dollar's sudden drop puts rate cuts in doubt: Thiessen report fingered as principal cause of selloff.
- Two Ontario plants included in GM's sale of four parts factories.
- Pamela Wallin aids Ontario investor push: TV host helps Premier Mike Harris to launch plan to sell province abroad.
- GM to announce sale of Ontario plants today.
- Popular tax shelter to be shut down: Ottawa changes rules for mutual fund limited partnerships.
